newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends down on U.S. dollar gains.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends down on U.S. dollar gains.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed weaker against its U.S. counterpart on Monday, in response to the U.S. dollar's persistent rise in major markets overseas, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.585, off an intra-day low of T$27.598 and against Saturday's T$27.570 finish.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$258 million.
The central bank's attitude also triggered U.S. dollar buying by importers, dealers said.
"The central bank's attitude plays an important role for the Taiwan dollar's recent falls," said one dealer.
Dealers have said the central bank's recent comments that the Taiwan dollar should follow the U.S. dollar's movements overseas, signalled further falls for the local currency.
"If the U.S. dollar remains strong overseas on Tuesday, the Taiwan dollar may fall below its recent support at T$27.60," the dealer said.
A range of T$27.57-62 was seen for Tuesday.
